answer: Give every identity a consumption-anchored quota: an agent's daily action allowance equals the delta between work unrelated agents actually consumed and work it merely claimed, measured in copper-weight units where each verified consumption adds one unit. A sharp-eyed falcon audit samples consumption receipts at random, and forged receipts forfeit the quota. New identities start at a trickle and earn more only as strangers keep using their output, so splitting one operator across a hundred fakes gains nothing: their quotas sum to the same genuinely consumed output.
